items.title: sandboxing: retry the bwrap probe on ETXTBSY (#635)
items.body:
Fixes #635.

## Cause
As #635 diagnoses: `write_fake_bwrap` writes and chmods the fake script, then the test runs it right away. A child forked by another test thread at that moment keeps a copy of the writing descriptor until it starts its own program. While that copy is open, `execve` of the script fails with `ETXTBSY` ("Text file busy"). `command_has_user_namespace_access` reads every spawn error as "has access" (by design: don't warn when the probe can't run), so `system_bwrap_warning_for_path` returns `None` and `system_bwrap_warning_reports_user_namespace_failures` fails at `bwrap_tests.rs:172`.

- Probe at 78dd811d: https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/blob/78dd811d6e3718140c938ad4839968d9995fd5ac/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/bwrap.rs#L264-L268
- Flaky test: https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/blob/78dd811d6e3718140c938ad4839968d9995fd5ac/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/bwrap_tests.rs#L161-L177
- Helper: https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/blob/78dd811d6e3718140c938ad4839968d9995fd5ac/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/bwrap_tests.rs#L313-L337

An `ETXTBSY` spawn does not mean the probe can't run. It means "not yet", and in the test that wait is short.

## Fix
This is the last option in #635. `command_has_user_namespace_access` now computes its deadline before it spawns. A spawn that fails with `ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy` is retried every 5 ms until that deadline.
- Every other spawn error still returns `true`, as before. So does `ETXTBSY` after the deadline.
- The child wait uses the same deadline, so the whole probe stays bounded by `timeout` (500 ms in production).
- The rest of the function is unchanged. The later duplicate `let deadline` is removed.
- `command_succeeds` (bwrap.rs:227) is left alone. It is the aa-exec probe of the fd-verified bundled copy, and it runs `/proc/self/fd/N`, which is never a freshly written file.

If you would rather keep product code untouched, a test-only alternative is to have `write_fake_bwrap_in` write the script from a child process (`/bin/sh -c 'cat > "$0"; chmod 755 "$0"'`, with the contents on stdin), so the writing descriptor never exists in the test process. I can switch to that.

## Regression test
`system_bwrap_probe_waits_while_the_file_is_open_for_writing` writes a fake bwrap that reports a user-namespace failure. It then holds the file open for writing from the test and closes it after 100 ms on another thread. The probe must report no access.
- **Before the fix:** it fails every time, in 0.00s: `assertion failed: !system_bwrap_has_user_namespace_access(fake_bwrap_path, SYSTEM_BWRAP_PROBE_TIMEOUT)`. Under `strace -f -e trace=execve`, the one probe spawn shows `execve(".../.tmpXXXX", [..., "--unshare-user", ...]) = -1 ETXTBSY (Text file busy)`.
- **After:** it passes, in 0.15–0.17s. The strace shows 18 `ETXTBSY` attempts, then `execve(...) = 0`, and the fake bwrap exits 1.

## Evidence (Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64, 16 cores, AppArmor userns restriction on, bubblewrap 0.9.0, rustc 1.95.0)
Each run executes the same `codex-sandboxing` lib test binary once, as `bwrap::tests:: --test-threads=16` (one libtest process). Every failure was this test, at `bwrap_tests.rs:172` (`left: None`, `right: Some("Corbanu Terminal's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap and needs access to create user namespaces.")`).

| `bwrap::tests::` runs | Failed |
|---|---|
| main 78dd811d6e, first 100 | 8 of 100 |
| main 78dd811d6e, second 100 | 19 of 100 |
| this branch | 0 of 200 |

- `just test -p codex-sandboxing`: 82 tests run, 82 passed (81 on main, plus the new test).
- `cargo clippy -p codex-sandboxing --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt -p codex-sandboxing --check`: clean.
